corroboration.hye_prior_pass: content_audit_log shows a register pass on hye_for_eng at 2026-08-14 09:41 UTC that converted 32 draft rows T→V in service scenes (e.g. go 142 'Կարո՞ղ ես ասել'→'Կարո՞ղ եք ասել'; go 157 'ունե՞ս'→'ունե՞ք'). Rows 149, 152 and 153 appear in the audit log only from the 09:27 translation insert — the 09:41 pass never touched them. The three rows fixed here are exactly that pass's residue.
corroboration.ell_tur_no_prior_pass: ell drafts were all written in a single batch at 09:30 and tur at 09:28; neither has a later register pass, so their state is the translator's original.

left_alone.why: Service scenes (2,3,7,8,9,11,12,14) are uniformly V (θα θέλατε / έχετε / μπορείτε / ορίστε ο καφές σας); peer scenes 4 and 6 are uniformly T (γεια σου / εσύ τι δουλειά κάνεις). Mechanical check for T-markers in service scenes returned 0 rows. Learner self-agreeing adjectives in drafts are already feminine (σίγουρη, χαρούμενη, ανήσυχη, χαζή), matching the female cast voice Αθηνά. No annotations.
Turkish and Armenian have no grammatical gender. Rule 2 is a structural no-op in both — not 'nothing found', but 'nothing findable'.
Zero rows match any of the eight annotation mark classes. Consistent with docs/a108/FINDINGS.md: the annotation defect lives in older released audio-backed content, not in these drafts.

left_alone.what: T-register in scenes 19/20/21 practice lines (ell go 187,192,193,199-205,208; hye go 187,199-205,208)
left_alone.why: Emotional and thanking lines with no clearly-named addressee. The brief's rule for 15-21 is 'most are general statements → T; V only if clearly addressed to a stranger/service person'. These are not clearly service-addressed, so T stands. Note tur renders the same scene-20 block in V — an internally-consistent divergence between languages, a judgment fork rather than a defect.

All draft rows in scene 6 are already T (go 25, 29, 32, 33, 34), correct for the canon's peer classification. The residual V forms in that scene sit on NON-draft rows (go 26, 28, 31, 36) and are out of scope.

gaps_and_decision_candidates.detail: Scene 22 Learner lines (go 221, 225, 231) use MASCULINE self-agreement — νευρικός, σίγουρος, χαρούμενος, έτοιμος — while the Learner cast voice is Αθηνά (female). This is a live rule-2 violation, but every one of those rows is target_text_draft = false, so the brief forbids touching them. Named, not fixed.
Scene 2 go 6 (Passenger, 'Παρακαλώ, κάτσε.') is the T imperative to a stranger — the exact defect fixed in tur go 6. It is non-draft in Greek, so out of scope.

Scene 1 (Neighbour, peer per canon) non-draft rows go 2/3 use siz ('Nasılsınız', 'gidiyorsunuz'). Canon says peer → T. Non-draft, so out of scope; and siz to an adult neighbour is defensible Turkish, so this is a decision candidate rather than a certain defect.

Scene 6 non-draft rows go 26/28/31/36 use Դուք/Ձեզ against the canon's peer→T classification, leaving that scene internally mixed (James asks 'քո անունը', Anna answers 'Իսկ Դուք'). Fixable only by touching non-draft rows.

Narrator number lines are inconsistently rendered: some spell numerals out (ell go 37 'Ένα. Δύο. Τρία.'), later ones leave digits (ell/tur/hye go 119, 140, 151+). A TTS-rendering concern for whoever generates this audio, not an A-108 rule.

go 7 'Şehir merkezine ne kadar uzakta?' reads slightly off (the idiom is closer to 'Şehir merkezi ne kadar uzakta?' / 'Şehir merkezine ne kadar var?'). Register-clean, so left; flagged for a quality pass.

confidence_statement: Greek and Turkish judgements are made to a confident non-native standard against the scene canon, the sibling-course renderings, and mechanical marker checks; the four writes are all structural T→V conversions on unambiguous 2nd-person morphology, not stylistic rewrites. Armenian is the language where I have least independent standing, and the three hye writes are therefore anchored to an external check rather than to my ear alone: they are precisely the rows the 2026-08-14 09:41 hye register pass left behind, converted the same direction and with the same orthographic convention that pass used. No line was changed on a judgement I could not corroborate.

verification.method: dry-run in a rolled-back transaction, then apply; both runs gate every UPDATE on the exact before-text AND target_text_draft, with pre- and post-flight assertions that abort on any drift
